draft.title: The Commonwealth budget
card: The Commonwealth budget is the federal government's yearly plan of how much money it expects to raise and how much it plans to spend. It is part of fiscal policy.
Changes to the budget affect aggregate demand, which is total spending in the economy. More government spending or lower taxes tend to raise it. Less spending or higher taxes tend to lower it.

Aggregate demand moves with the business cycle, the pattern of faster and slower growth over time. The government can use the budget to steady it. In a slowdown it can add spending or cut taxes. When growth is too strong it can cut spending or raise taxes.
Monetary policy, which is run by the Reserve Bank, is used alongside the budget for the same aim of steadying aggregate demand.
draft.remember: The budget is the yearly plan of revenue and spending, used with monetary policy to steady aggregate demand.

a.q: Why might the government plan more spending in the budget during a slowdown?
opts: To lift aggregate demand and support growth
To lower aggregate demand and slow growth
To cut the cost of borrowing set by the Reserve Bank
To stop the business cycle from happening at all
a.why: More government spending tends to raise aggregate demand, which supports growth when the economy is slow. Lowering demand is the wrong direction, as that suits a period of strong growth. The budget can steady the cycle, but it does not stop it.
a.clue: Think about which way spending moves total demand.

b.q: Growth in Australia is strong and aggregate demand is rising faster than the economy can supply goods. Which budget plan best fits the aim of steadying demand?
opts: Cut planned spending or raise taxes
Raise planned spending and cut taxes
Leave the budget alone and rely on the business cycle
Hand control of the budget to the Reserve Bank
b.why: When demand is too strong, less spending or higher taxes tend to lower it, which steadies the economy. Raising spending and cutting taxes would push demand up further. The Reserve Bank uses monetary policy alongside the budget, but it does not take over the budget.
b.clue: The aim is to slow demand, so which way should spending and taxes move?

a.best: To lift aggregate demand and support growth

b.best: Cut planned spending or raise taxes
